items.title: Here's How Many Shares of Procter & Gamble You'd Need for $1,000 in Yearly Dividends
items.summary: Even if generating $1,000 in dividend payouts from Procter & Gamble isn't in an investor's budget, it's still a stock worthy of investment consideration.

items.title: The Average 1-Year CD Pays Just 1.76%. These Dividend Stocks Could Pay More
items.summary: A guaranteed bank rate sounds safe until you weigh what it can't do. Six blue-chip payers offer income that can grow, but a board can cut it at any meeting, and the tax bill may decide which side comes out ahead.

items.title: 4 Dividend Raisers With Balance Sheets Strong Enough to Keep Raising Through Any Downturn
items.summary: When profits dip, lenders get paid first and the dividend is usually what gets cut. Four household names have raised their payouts year after year, and one of them holds a credit rating almost no other U.S. company can match.

items.title: Coca-Cola vs P&G: Staples Rotation Crowns a Clear Income Winner
items.summary: Tech is bleeding while soda and detergent makers rally, and Jim Cramer wants to camp out in staples "for a bit." Two dividend legends have very different runs behind them, and only one suits someone living off portfolio income.

items.title: Rate Hikes Could Be Coming: History Likes These 4 Consumer Staples Stocks
items.summary: The Fed ended its pause, and traders now price in another hike by December. Three past tightening cycles reveal which household-name staples stocks protected portfolios, and one of them beat the market every single time.

items.title: Procter & Gamble vs. Colgate-Palmolive: Which Dividend Stock Is Safer?
items.summary: Both consumer giants beat earnings, yet their margins are moving in opposite directions as oil prices climb and a cautious U.S. shopper holds back. One dividend carries a thin balance sheet buffer, and retirees need to know which one.

items.title: General Mills Just Gained 15% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGeneral Mills is up 15% in the past month, lifted by Procter & Gamble’s and Kraft Heinz’s quarterly reports while tech stocks sold off. General Mills had no news of its own behind the move, and Campbell’s ran even further.

items.title: 3 Dependable Dividend Stocks for a $250,000 Passive Income Strategy
items.summary: One of these dividend payers slashed its quarterly check in 2022, and another has a stock that has gone nowhere in five years. Why would a retiree still trust them with a third of a $250,000 income plan?
